summary: Conflict, economic decline and climate shocks, worsened by shrinking operating space and funding gaps, mean 23.1 million people (about two thirds of the population) need aid in 2026. Prices and inflation keep eroding incomes, and damage to Red Sea ports plus sanctions and import limits have caused shortages of food, fuel and electricity in areas under de facto authorities. More than 18 million face acute food insecurity, 2.5 million children under five are acutely malnourished, and over 3,000 nutrition sites have closed. Over 16 million people need protection help, including 4.7 million who are displaced.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Yemen Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: Overlapping gaps in nutrition, education, housing and water keep food insecurity high and leave households exposed to price, seasonal and displacement shocks. More than 2.61 million Afghans returned in 2025, most involuntarily and without assets or documents, straining host communities that were already near their limits. Women face the sharpest economic exclusion, as restrictions on their rights, formalised by a 2024 law on public conduct, limit their access to public life and work.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Afghanistan Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: After a dire funding year in 2025, aid agencies narrowed their response to 17 priority localities, mainly in Darfur and Kordofan plus Khartoum and Aj Jazirah, where needs are worst and delivery is possible. Needs are expected to stay alarmingly high, yet the 2026 plan covers only the most severe areas and leaves at least 14.2 million people outside the scope of the response. Khartoum and Aj Jazirah became more accessible during 2025.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Sudan Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: OCHA expects needs to stay extremely high in 2026 even though fighting has eased overall and the number of displacement sites has fallen. Returning refugees and displaced people may change where and what kind of help is needed, and prioritisation is tight because of funding limits. Escalating hostilities in As-Sweida, spilling into Dar'a and Rural Damascus, created a new caseload of 492,860 people in need in the south.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Syria Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: An estimated 3.6 million people are displaced by conflict and the earthquake, the highest figure on record, and most have fled more than once and shelter informally with little access to food, health care or clean water. The 2026 plan focuses on the two thirds of the country hit by those shocks, where 16.2 million people (including 5 million children) need life-saving help. OCHA stresses that the lower figure than in 2025 comes from a narrower scope, not from any improvement.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Myanmar Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: Conflict, climate shocks and disease outbreaks drive the crisis. A prolonged drought in the north after weak 2025 rains is worsening hunger and water shortages, and weak autumn rains are forecast to raise needs further. About 4.4 million people face acute food insecurity, including 921,000 in emergency conditions (up 35 per cent on 2024), and 1.85 million children are expected to be acutely malnourished. Measles, cholera and malaria are spreading while funding shortfalls cut response coverage.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Somalia Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: Over 10 million people, two thirds of the population, need help in a crisis OCHA ties to unresolved political turmoil, violence, economic collapse, disease and climate shocks, with extra pressure from people crossing over from Sudan. More than 7.5 million are projected to face crisis-level hunger or worse in the 2026 lean season, 2.1 million children are expected to be acutely malnourished, and 2.6 million people remain displaced. Floods have hit over a million people every year since 2019.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA South Sudan Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: Civilians across Ukraine face repeated missile and drone strikes that cause mass-casualty incidents, destroy homes and cut essential services. Shifts in the front line in 2025 caused new displacement, with more than 130,000 people evacuated with government or humanitarian support. Older people and people with disabilities often stay behind in front-line areas and depend on aid, while transit centres and collective sites run beyond capacity.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Ukraine Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: The UN and partners are asking for $4.06 billion to help 3.6 million people in need across the occupied Palestinian territory, citing the scale of death, destruction and deprivation in Gaza. Since the ceasefire took effect on 10 October, more supplies have entered Gaza and aid groups have expanded services, but bureaucratic obstacles, access restrictions and hostile rhetoric toward the UN still limit humanitarian space. About 201 UN agencies, NGOs and Red Cross and Red Crescent organisations coordinate the response.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA occupied Palestinian territory Flash Appeal 2026

summary: OCHA describes a severe and worsening crisis: hostilities have continued despite ceasefire announcements, causing ongoing displacement, limiting access and blocking safe returns, with shelters overstretched and infrastructure badly damaged. Livelihoods, especially in agriculture and small business, are disrupted and tensions are rising. Between 2 March and 31 May partners reached more than 680,000 people; the revised appeal asks for an extra $331.5 million for June to August, bringing the total to $639.9 million, of which $185.9 million had been received by the end of May.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Lebanon Flash Appeal 2026 (revised, June 2026)

summary: The conflict is reshaping and spreading as armed groups fragment and seek territorial control: about 78 per cent of the rural population (9.9 million people) lives under the influence of at least one non-state armed group. In 2025, 1.5 million people were affected by conflict and violence, three times the 2024 figure, with roughly one displacement a day and one confinement every three days; Catatumbo alone had a third of all displaced people. Violations against children have risen for a fifth year, and climate disasters and the needs of refugees and migrants add to the pressure.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Colombia Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: Economic and political shifts, limited access to foreign currency and sharp price rises for essentials are pushing needs up, with inflation projected to reach triple digits. A basic food basket for a family of five is estimated at $586, far beyond most households, and gaps in health care, water, education and energy persist. Limited public spending, climate events and weak access to income support hit women, children, older people, people with disabilities and Indigenous communities hardest; 7.9 million people need assistance.
basis: OCHA 2026 response plan text, paraphrased
source_title: OCHA Venezuela Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026

summary: Armed violence keeps displacing people: IOM's tracking update of 17 November covers displacement in the Croix-des-Bouquets commune between 18 October and 13 November, and OCHA publishes weekly situation updates for the region. OCHA's plan notes that University Hospital La Paix is the only public hospital in the capital still offering advanced care, a lifeline for more than two million people in the metropolitan area. Aid groups say they are trying to make the response less bureaucratic and closer to Haitian communities, with more direct funding to national organisations.
basis: OCHA 2026 plan text and latest report headlines, summarised
source_title: OCHA Haiti Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026; IOM and OCHA reports

summary: In 2026 aid partners aim to reach 3.8 million people, about 15 per cent of the population and 75 per cent of those in need, 19 per cent fewer than last year because the count of people in need fell (mainly through method changes) and because delivery capacity is limited. The response concentrates on saving lives, protection and livelihoods in the highest-need areas of northern and central Mali. OCHA published a joint humanitarian overview for Burkina Faso, Mali and western Niger as of 23 October 2026.
basis: OCHA 2026 plan text and latest report headlines, summarised
source_title: OCHA Mali Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026; OCHA regional overview

summary: Under the global push to streamline and localise aid, Niger's 2026 plan keeps tight prioritisation and plans more direct funding and responsibility for national and local organisations. In mid-2025, 77 humanitarian organisations were operating there, 31 per cent fewer than in 2024. On 10 November UNHCR reported that tens of thousands of people who fled violence in Nigeria face a growing crisis in Niger.
basis: OCHA 2026 plan text and latest report headlines, summarised
source_title: OCHA Niger Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026; UNHCR

summary: With resources sharply reduced, the 2026 plan targets 2.5 million people across the conflict-hit north-east states of Borno, Adamawa and Yobe with life-saving and protection aid, and aims for a locally led response by 2028, with government funding expected to be the main source. Health needs are rising: on 16 November Médecins Sans Frontières warned that shortages of diphtheria treatment put thousands of children at risk, and the Red Cross reports a 2026 diphtheria outbreak.
basis: OCHA 2026 plan text and latest report headlines, summarised
source_title: OCHA Nigeria Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026; MSF and IFRC

summary: Cameroon is one of eight countries moving from an internationally led aid system to one led by national and local actors under the Humanitarian Reset, even as needs stay high. OCHA says years of underfunding and sharp donor cuts in 2025 have limited the response and calls for stronger advocacy so people are not forgotten. A cholera outbreak is under way: UNICEF issued its fifth flash update for 24 September to 23 October and the Red Cross activated an early action protocol on 7 October.
basis: OCHA 2026 plan text and latest report headlines, summarised
source_title: OCHA Cameroon Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026; UNICEF and IFRC

summary: Conflict in Cabo Delgado keeps deteriorating and drought has hit other regions. OCHA's review of 2025 found that funding fell so far the plan had to be cut to a few priority districts, and by mid-year its clusters had only 1 to 28 per cent of requirements, with assistance mostly limited to food. In November, IOM reported a new wave of violence in the north that displaced more than 7,000 people, and the famine early-warning network expects crisis-level food insecurity to emerge in the centre as stocks run down.
basis: OCHA 2026 plan text and latest report headlines, summarised
source_title: OCHA Mozambique Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026; IOM and FEWS NET

summary: A joint plan led by the national disaster and dyke management authority with the UN and the Red Cross responds to a run of typhoons and floods, setting out the most urgent humanitarian and recovery needs of the affected provinces. The plan counts about 1.4 million people in need and 0.7 million targeted, and stresses investing in risk-informed development, anticipatory action and disaster risk reduction so communities recover with more resilience.
basis: OCHA 2026 plan text and latest report headlines, summarised
source_title: OCHA Viet Nam Joint Response Plan (multiple typhoons and floods, Oct 2025 - Jun 2026)

summary: Aid-sector reporting on Burkina Faso is thin, about three reports a week, but recent items show the response continuing: OCHA's joint humanitarian overview for Burkina Faso, Mali and western Niger (23 October 2026), a funding overview for the 2026 response plan (30 October), a WFP country brief for October and monthly education cluster meetings. The famine early-warning network noted a rainy season ending with deficits in neighbouring Niger and Chad.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: OCHA, WFP, FEWS NET and UN agencies via ReliefWeb

summary: The Central African Republic's response continues alongside pressure from the Sudan crisis: UNHCR published refugee and asylum-seeker statistics (30 September 2026) and a Sudan situation update (10 November), and OCHA released its inter-sectoral humanitarian dashboard for January to August 2026. The UN peacekeeping mission published a piece on 12 November arguing the country is a peacekeeping success story, while clusters such as logistics keep meeting in Bangui.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: OCHA, UNHCR and UN mission reports via ReliefWeb

summary: Chad is receiving people fleeing Sudan: UNHCR published an emergency update on arrivals on 15 November, and OCHA described the humanitarian situation in the east as of 3 November. Aid groups are also reporting on the Lac region (30 October) and a dengue outbreak that the Red Cross is responding to. Alongside the national plan, a separate refugee response plan covers about 1.1 million refugees.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: UNHCR, OCHA, IFRC and cluster reports via ReliefWeb

summary: DR Congo has the most aid-sector reporting of any crisis here, about 35 reports a week. Recent items cover epidemics (a cholera epidemiological report for week 44, polio eradication work and a health cluster response), a monthly displacement report for eastern DR Congo for October from Mercy Corps, and OCHA's weekly regional events briefing. An OCHA photo caption notes that a Goma site sheltering over 71,000 people who fled fighting in North Kivu was dismantled soon after January 2025.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: OCHA, WHO, Mercy Corps and cluster reports via ReliefWeb

summary: Drought is the main current story: OCHA issued a drought flash appeal on 22 September, and the famine early-warning network says staple losses, limited income and an early lean season are driving crisis-level food insecurity (IPC Phase 3) through May 2027. South Korea announced drought assistance, and IOM published an assessment of Hondurans who returned voluntarily on their own. Honduras gets few reports, about 1.6 a week, and the needs figure used here is from 2025, so treat its rank with care.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: OCHA, FEWS NET, FAO and IOM reports via ReliefWeb

summary: OCHA's plan counts 2.8 million people in need and 1.9 million targeted for 2026. Recent reporting centres on people returning from Iran (joint IOM and UNHCR border monitoring and flash updates on arrests and detention up to 7 November), drought in Tharparkar district in Sindh (Red Cross, 9 November), a WFP country brief and a World Bank water and sanitation project for 1.5 million people in rural Sindh.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: OCHA, IOM, UNHCR, IFRC, WFP reports via ReliefWeb

summary: OCHA's 2026 plan counts 4.2 million people in need and 2.0 million targeted. A year after Hurricane Melissa, Red Cross reports describe recovery in the hardest-hit provinces such as Granma, supported by aid and energy solutions, and OCHA publishes monthly monitoring of the UN action plan (September report on 3 November). A final report on an arboviral outbreak was also published.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: OCHA, IFRC and plan-tracker reports via ReliefWeb and humanitarianaction.info

summary: Cyclones Fytia and Gezani struck early in 2026, and a UN flash appeal of $67.8 million aimed to help 486,000 of 581,000 people in need. The focus now is hunger: the famine early-warning network expects a prolonged crisis across the Grand South as an early lean season and rising prices deepen food insecurity, and CARE warns El Niño could make it worse. Madagascar receives only about 1.5 reports a week.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: OCHA, ECHO, WFP, FEWS NET and CARE via ReliefWeb

summary: Flash floods in Rasuwa in early September affected an estimated 84,270 people, including 32,021 children, across 17 municipalities in six districts. A UN and government flash appeal launched on 4 September asks for $49.6 million to support more than 84,000 people over four months. The Nepal Red Cross is publishing regular situation reports and a 12 November story describes survivors racing to rebuild before winter.
basis: Latest aid-sector report headlines (ReliefWeb, to 17 Nov 2026), summarised
source_title: UNICEF, Nepal Red Cross, UNFPA and WFP reports via ReliefWeb
